lines.en: What most conflicts need is not a winner, but a listener both sides can trust.
It is remarkable how many wars begin over words that were never actually said.
Were both sides to state the other's position fairly, half the argument would end on its own.
However deep the grievance, the conversation must begin somewhere, and someone must begin it.
Not until the guns fall silent can the harder work of peace begin.
It is said that you do not make peace with your friends; you make it with your enemies.
What the mediator wrote on one page, after ten years of fighting, was simply what each side feared losing.
The apology arrived fifty years late, which is to say, it arrived.
Little is solved by winning an argument with someone who must then live with the defeat.
Rarely does the first offer end a conflict; it merely proves that ending it is possible.
What the treaty left unresolved returned, fifteen years later, wearing a different flag.
It is not weakness to listen first; it is the only strength that matters at the table.
Were every side to write the history of the conflict, the maps would not match, but the tears would.
Not until the grandchildren of enemies study in the same classroom can a conflict be called finished.
However just the cause, the methods by which it is fought become part of what it finally wins.
